item.title: Cornell's Jane Doe is 'terrified' after police swatting incident, lawyer says
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
The Cornell University campus on the night of October 6, 2026. Student leaders held a town hall to discuss fallout from the Jane Doe sexual assault case. - Surya Vaidy/CNN One month ago, the woman now known to America as Cornell’s Jane Doe was living in New York City among thousands of other aspirational twentysomethings, attempting to break into the hotel industry and build a new life, according to her attorney, Thomas Giuffra. But that plan has been derailed since she filed a lawsuit against Cornell University and others, alleging she was raped at a frat house in 2024. Instead, Giuffra said, Doe spent Wednesday taping up paper to obscure the windows of her parents’ home out of fear that a gunman could attack her, and reeling from a swatting episode that he said prompted police to swarm their home Tuesday night with weapons drawn. Doe is increasingly scared for her own safety, Giuffra said in a phone interview with CNN on Wednesday as he detailed his client’s deteriorating mental state after an escalating series of violent threats. Officers pointed weapons at Jane Doe’s boyfriend, her brother and her father after receiving a bogus tip that “someone was killing people in the house” on Tuesday evening, he said. Death threats, doxxing attempts and an outpouring of anger online have also been levied at his client, Giuffra added. “I don’t think she’s in a good spot now,” Giuffra said. “She’s scared.” The public fallout from her allegations have rocked one of the country’s leading educational institutions. The university, its campus police force and the Tompkins County District Attorney’s office have each faced scrutiny over how they initially investigated her claims. Anger among students was palpable during a Wednesday sit-in on the Ithaca, New York, campus. Cornell students take part in a seven-hour sit-in protest on Wednesday. - Angelina Katsanis/Reuters Doe herself has been following media reports and social media posts on her case, Giuffra told CNN as he described a family reeling from a sudden and terrifying ordeal that punctured their sense of safety. “Before (this week), it was just a lunatic fringe, which you can be dismissive of,” he said. “Now it’s somebody taking real steps to harm you, and that’s pretty frightening.” Doe’s parents are furious after a fake tip to police, lawyer says At 7 p.m. on Tuesday evening, a police officer in Doe’s hometown was dispatched to respond to a disturbing call: A man had shot and killed his mother and then turned the gun on his sister. The information was bogus. But the officer, believing an active-shooter situation was unfolding, rushed to Doe’s home, where he saw a car backing out from the driveway, according to a police report from the incident obtained by CNN. As he apprehended the two men in the vehicle – later revealed to be Doe’s brother and her boyfriend – another figure emerged from the home’s doorway. “I’m the dad. What’s going on?” he yelled, according to the report. The man told police his daughter is Jane Doe of the Cornell case and that the family was “being threatened by numerous unknown people.” The swatting incident was an escalation in a series of threats to Doe’s safety that have roiled her family this week. The term “swatting” refers to false tips made to law enforcement agencies with the intention of having armed officers deployed to somebody’s home or place of business. “Luckily the brother was in his car, (he) put his hands up,” Giuffra told CNN on Wednesday, relaying the events of the night. “(Doe’s) boyfriend got thrown on the ground,” and her father also had “guns put in his face,” according to Giuffra. “If you had a trigger-happy cop, or somebody had done the wrong thing, somebody could have ended up dead,” he said. Police are now investigating the swatting attempt, and the FBI is also looking into the events, according to Giuffra. According to Doe’s lawyer and two police reports reviewed by CNN, police arrived moments after Doe received a separate phone call from somebody claiming to share a first name with one of the seven men she named in her civil complaint. According to her account to officers in the reports, Doe “began panicking” when she received the call, “because (her phone) wouldn’t stop ringing.” She informed officers about that previous call while they were at her house following the swatting tip. Before the night was over, Giuffra’s wife told him that she, too, had received a threatening phone call. “These people have done so much research into (Doe),” Giuffra said. It is not clear whether the separate threats cited in the police reports were connected. Giuffra said he was in contact with Doe and her family on Wednesday. Her parents are angry and she is terrified, he said. The lawyer shared with CNN an audio recording of a call he says was placed to his office on Wednesday afternoon. In the recording, a man identifies himself as “the person who called your client.” The man also is heard saying: “I’m telling you guys simply, I think you should advise your client to withdraw the case. Otherwise blood will be shed.” Doxxing attempts also have taken their toll Tuesday’s swatting attack was an escalation of the potential dangers facing Doe since she filed her lawsuit last month, but it was far from the only threat she’s received, her lawyer said. Giuffra estimated that dozens of threats have been made against her since mid-September, when his client filed a 101-page complaint alleging she had been sexually assaulted and raped by several members of the Xi chapter of Cornell’s Chi Phi fraternity. The Chi Phi fraternity house on the campus of Cornell University. - Surya Vaidy/CNN Doe’s civil suit was filed against the university, the fraternity, seven fraternity members and others. It alleges that members of the frat drugged and sexually assaulted her in October 2024 and invited other fraternity members in a group chat to join the assault. The suit also alleges the school failed to protect her and adequately punish the accused students, who all deny wrongdoing. Giuffra detailed to CNN another threat: a text message, sent to Doe’s phone on Monday, with three emojis depicting guns. Meanwhile, a handful of online personalities with large followings have led a campaign to uncover the identity of Doe, whose name was redacted in legal documents. One wrote on X to 347,000 followers in late September: “If you happen to know who this Cornell ‘Jane Doe’ is, get in touch and I would be happy to publish her name and identifying information.” He later claimed to have identified her and said he shared that identity online before deleting his post. Such behavior is known as doxxing, or sharing someone’s personal information or identity online without their permission. It has left Doe frightened and struggling to come to terms with the impact of the lawsuit, which has prompted outrage and scrutiny of how the university and its private police force initially investigated her claims. On Wednesday, Doe was “taping paper over windows in the house she’s lived at her whole life,” Giuffra said, “so people can’t see into her house to take a shot at her.” “I don’t get shook up very easily, but this shook me up. I didn’t want to have a body on my hands,” he said. “The dad is … concerned for his daughter. He can’t believe this has happened out of something where she’s just trying to stand up for herself and be heard,” Giuffra added. “But the parents are really strong people, and they’re going to protect their daughter.” Her career dream is ‘lost’ Doe had studied hotel administration at Cornell’s prestigious Nolan School of Hotel Administration, and it had been her “dream” to attend the school, Giuffra said. Her complaint says she traveled across the country and arrived at the school with the same “hopes, expectations and trepidations of other high school graduates.” But she left the program without graduating after the alleged assault took place two years ago. Doe initially attempted to begin a career in New York City earlier this year, but after filing the lawsuit – “when everything hit the fan” – she instead returned to her family home, where she has been staying with her boyfriend, her lawyer said. “The dream is lost,” Giuffra told CNN, referring to her hopes of working in the hospitality industry. Instead, Doe has been hiding out at her parents’ home, where she has been following the intense media coverage of her case. “It’s kind of hard to switch it off,” Giuffra said. “She comes from a generation of people who are focused on social media.” CNN is not specifying the location of Doe’s family home at her lawyer’s request. She has been going on walks but otherwise spends much of her time indoors. She remains in contact with some of the friends she made at Cornell, Giuffra said. Cornell students Tuesday on the school's grounds in Ithaca, New York. - Surya Vaidy/CNN “She’s a little paranoid,” Giuffra said of his client. “If she’s out of (the) safety zone of her family, she just doesn’t seem to function well.” A few friends of the family know she has returned home and have been providing support, and Doe’s mother has taken time off from work to help look after her daughter, he said. Doe is also aware of the many messages of support that she has received from around the world since filing the lawsuit, according to Giuffra. Cornell, which recently appointed former acting US Attorney General Sally Yates to investigate the school’s handling of sexual assault claims, was the site of a seven-hour sit-in on Wednesday to show “solidarity with Jane Doe,” according to flyers for the event. During a meeting with Cornell’s Graduate and Professional Student Assembly on Monday, university President Michael Kotlikoff acknowledged the mounting frustration across campus as more details and questions emerge about Doe’s 2024 allegations. “We’re all angry. I understand that anger,” Kotlikoff said, according to the independent student newspaper the Cornell Daily Sun. “People want easy answers to this.” The school’s president previously released a video statement promising further review of the case, saying it highlights “heartbreaking and troubling issues about sexual assault, dehumanization, and aspects of party culture, alcohol, and drug use.” “The students up there (at Cornell) have been overwhelmingly supportive, and it’s wonderful,” Giuffra said. “They’re trying to effect change, and bringing out to the light something that’s been going on for generations.” For more CNN news and newsletters create an account at CNN.com This article originally appeared on CNN at https://www.cnn.com/2026/10/08/us/cornell-jane-doe-threats-swatting

The USS Abraham Lincoln near the city of Pattaya in Thailand on 6 September 2026. Photograph: Chanakarn Laosarakham/AFP/Getty Images The USS Abraham Lincoln, the US aircraft carrier that has been deployed for nearly a year and has spent months supporting US military operations against Iran, is scheduled to dock in San Diego on Thursday afternoon. It marks the end of a deployment that has been described as “one of the most operationally intense and consequential of the modern era” and that became marked by a record-setting stretch at sea, repeated deployment extensions, and reports of supply shortages and deteriorating morale and mental health among some crew members. The Lincoln left San Diego last November, initially bound for the Pacific. But it was redirected to the Middle East after the US and Israel launched their war with Iran in late February. The carrier remained there until late August, when it was relieved by the USS George Washington and began its journey home . Earlier in August, the Lincoln’s deployment made headlines and faced scrutiny as reports began surfacing about poor living conditions onboard the ship, including shortages of supplies and water, plumbing problems, low morale and worsening mental health among the roughly 5,000 personnel on the carrier. Two leading military newspapers also reported that there had been two attempts by sailors to jump overboard, causing concern among families and military health experts. The reports prompted outrage from Democrats , while senior officials in the Trump administration pushed back . Pete Hegseth, the US defense secretary, called the reports “completely misrepresented ”, and when reporters asked Donald Trump if he thought the deployment had gone on too long, he responded : “Not nearly long enough” – a comment that angered some naval families. In a statement at the time, Adm Brad Cooper, who heads US Central Command, claimed that of the US navy’s 11 active aircraft carriers, the Lincoln had “among the lowest number of cases related to mental health”. But he said that “this doesn’t mean that all is perfect”. Cooper said that a long deployment at sea “is uniquely challenging and tough, and every single one of us, including me, reacts to stressors in different ways”. Two weeks ago, as the Lincoln headed back to San Diego, Hung Cao, the acting navy secretary, acknowledged that eight service members from the Lincoln and its accompanying strike group attempted to take their own lives. Sara Jacobs, a Democrat representing California’s 51st district who visited the Lincoln in late September, said in a statement last week that while she is “relieved that the USS Abraham Lincoln will soon be back in San Diego” and “looking forward to welcoming them home”, her “demand for accountability won’t end when they make port”. “I will continue pushing for an [office of the inspector general] investigation into these conditions and a House armed services committee field hearing in San Diego to hear directly from these service members,” she said. “We need to prevent this crisis from happening ever again, and ultimately end the Iran war and bring all our service members home.” On Wednesday, Hegseth visited the Lincoln ahead of its return, and praised the crew. He acknowledged that their deployment had not been “easy”. “When you greet your families tomorrow, just pass my gratitude from the president and myself,” Hegseth said. “Let them know that their long wait, we believe, was in service of a righteous and historic mission.” During his remarks, Hegseth announced that those onboard the vessel would be awarded the presidential unit citation, which, according to the US military , is conferred on units of the armed forces “for extraordinary heroism in action against an armed enemy”. Ahead of the Lincoln’s arrival on Thursday afternoon, Blue Star Families, one of the largest US-based non-profit organizations supporting active military service members, veterans and their families, said in a statement that “every homecoming is an important moment for military families”. The organization said that it “welcomes home the sailors of USS Abraham Lincoln and wants every family to know they’re not alone as they reconnect”. In the weeks ahead, Blue Star Families said it will host appreciation days for Lincoln sailors and their families, including several events next month in San Diego. By Luc Cohen NEW YORK, Oct 8 (Reuters) - Ousted Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores both were hit with an additional US criminal charge on Thursday stemming from accusations they tortured political opponents and American citizens to retain their grip on power in ‌the South American country. Maduro and Flores were charged with an additional count of conspiracy to commit torture in addition to the drug ‌trafficking charges they previously faced, according to a superseding indictment filed in Manhattan federal court. Flores, 69, and Maduro, 63, were captured by the US military on January 3 in their Caracas home and ​brought to New York to face the drug charges. Venezuela has since boosted cooperation with the US under the leadership of Maduro's former Vice President Delcy Rodriguez. Relations between the United States and oil-rich Venezuela were tense during the socialist Maduro's 13 years in power. US officials and human rights groups have long accused Venezuelan officials of torturing detainees, but Thursday's indictment marked the first time Maduro faced criminal charges over the allegations. In one instance, prosecutors said Maduro in 2013 ordered the arrest of a Venezuelan military officer ‌he suspected of planning a coup. Members of Venezuela's military ⁠counterintelligence directorate then interrogated the officer while shocking the individual with a live electric wire around 20 times and hung the individual by the hands and feet for several minutes at a time, prosecutors said. In 2022, an American citizen detained while ⁠entering Venezuela was accused of conspiring to assassinate Maduro and was tortured by military counterintelligence officers through beatings and shocks to the person's arms, legs and genitals, according to the indictment. Maduro's lawyers did not immediately respond to a request for comment. During a court hearing on Thursday over Flores' push to be released from jail, her lawyer Mark ​Donnelly ​said he had not had time to review the new charges with Flores. Flores was ​not asked to enter a plea. Maduro and Flores pleaded not ‌guilty to the drug charges and have been held at Brooklyn's Metropolitan Detention Center since their capture. Their trial is scheduled for June 1, 2027. FLORES SEEKS RELEASE FROM JAIL Separately, Flores appeared in a US court on Thursday to urge US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein to release her from jail for health reasons while she awaits her drug trafficking trial next year. Flores' lawyers said their client needs a cardiac procedure and wants to recover in a more comfortable environment. The lawyers proposed moving her to a residence in the New York City area with round-the-clock private security, and said she is not a danger to the community. Hellerstein ‌said Flores, who wore a dark prison t-shirt and a headset to listen to a ​simultaneous Spanish translation of the proceedings, appears to be relatively healthy. "For whatever it's worth, her ​appearance today is no worse and perhaps a little better than when ​I first met with her on her arraignment," Hellerstein said, referring to her first appearance in court on January 5. "She ‌was still bandaged up from the military invasion," Hellerstein said. Prosecutors in ​the Manhattan US Attorney's Office oppose ​Flores' release. They said Flores has received adequate medical care at the detention center, and if released poses an "extreme" risk of flight and danger to the public, including possible witness intimidation. Prosecutors also said other judges have found it unfair to let some criminal defendants pay for their own out-of-jail supervision, because defendants of ​lesser means cannot afford it. Hellerstein's bail decision will not ‌affect Flores' trial or potential punishment. If convicted, she faces a mandatory minimum 40-year sentence. Flores was Venezuela's attorney general and led its National ​Assembly before becoming first lady. US prosecutors say she took hundreds of thousands of dollars in bribes from a large drug trafficker. Texas has taken center stage ahead of next month’s midterm elections as Democrats grow more optimistic about their chances in the state up and down the ballot. For months, the state’s highly contested Senate race has dominated midterm elections headlines, but Democrats say they are seeing opportunity in other Texas contests as well. The Democratic Governors Association and Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker (D) announced this week they each plan to give $1 million to support Democrat Gina Hinojosa in the state’s gubernatorial race. Meanwhile, leaked audio of Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton blaming the national GOP as Democrat James Talarico leads in the polls has rocked the Senate race. Still, President Trump and Vice President Vance have traveled multiple times to the state to bolster Lone Star State Republicans in competitive contests. Trump is set to rally alongside Paxton and Republican House candidate Carlos De La Cruz in San Antonio Wednesday evening. “Texas is clearly in play,” said Brendan Steinhauser, a Texas-based GOP strategist who ran Sen. John Cornyn’s (R-Texas) 2014 reelection bid. “Republicans understand they have a real threat they need to defend against, and Democrats see a real opportunity where they can go on offense, and potentially win a U.S. Senate seat and maybe even the governor’s race as well," he added. A New York Times/Siena University poll from Saturday showed Talarico with a 7 percentage point lead over Paxton, while Hinojosa edged out Texas Gov. Greg Abbott by 3 points. “I think we waited too long to send in the cavalry,” Paxton donor Dan Eberhart said when asked about the state of the race. On Wednesday, another leak of Paxton's remarks from a closed-door fundraiser surfaced, with the state attorney general blaming the Iran war and high gas prices for his standing in the polls. “It’s not tariffs. … It’s the war, it’s gas prices, it’s diesel,” Paxton told donors and lobbyists at a closed-door fundraiser, according to audio obtained by Axios. A spokesperson for Paxton’s campaign told the outlet that the development is a “non-story,” adding that Paxton acknowledged “what every Texan already knows: gas and diesel prices are too high.” One Republican strategist blasted Paxton’s remarks to donors as “hugely problematic.” “Why would you say those things? I mean, it’s just unimaginable, to be honest, that you would let your guard down that much and say things that hurt your standing, the president’s standing, and frankly just feeds into an already challenging narrative,” the strategist said. Steinhauser called the intraparty squabbling “unhelpful.” “This is not the time to be doing that,” Steinhauser said. "I don’t want to see Republicans out there starting the blame game. I think that creates a psychology of losing. It creates a psychology of depressing turnout.” “There definitely is sort of an undercurrent of potential blame game that’s already starting,” he added. Other Republicans warn the Senate race’s drama could have a detrimental impact on the state’s House races, as Democrats seek to win back control of the lower chamber in November. “It is important that Paxton wins,” Eberhart said. “A Paxton loss likely brings with it six House losses.” Texas is home to six competitive House races this cycle in the 9th, 15th, 23rd, 28th, 34th and 35th districts.
